New-Gen Feature Coming to Apple Maps, Making ETAs More Accurate Than in Google Maps
6 photos
Photo: Bogdan Popa/autoevolution
Navigation apps are getting all kinds of new-gen gimmicks, such as aerial views and cyclist warnings, but Apple is working on something that will certainly come in handy for drivers.
The fruit-named company is reportedly preparing parking-aware ETAs, which means that the application would take into account the time you spend parking and walking to calculate your ETA. This means you’ll get more accurate ETAs than in any other application, such as Waze, where the time of arrival is exclusively based on traffic conditions to reach a destination.
Like all the other navigation apps out there, Apple Maps uses a simple system to determine your ETA to a destination.
When you define the address where you want to drive, Apple Maps checks the distance, speed limits, and traffic data to determine how much time you’ll spend on the road to the destination. This ETA refers exclusively to the time you spend behind the wheel going from point A to point B, without considering any other factors, such as the time you spend when you park your car.
That’s going to change if a feature that Apple is currently working on behind closed doors makes its way to the production channel.
Photo: Bogdan Popa/autoevolution A recent post on X from @itspdfu indicates that Apple is developing a feature that would measure how long you spend near your destination for parking and how much time you add to your journey walking to the destination. This is possible using background location and motion data, so your iPhone would collect the necessary data to determine how much time you need to reach a destination in addition to the driving time.
This feature comes in handy for two reasons. The first one is related to the parking job, as finding a parking spot in a busy area isn’t always easy. Apple Maps could collect data related to parking and offer an estimated time of arrival that would also include such information, making it easier for users to determine the time when they will arrive at the destination - when this destination is not a location on the street but a building or another location not reachable by car.
For example, if you need to arrive at a meeting at an office building, Apple Maps would also take into account the parking time and how much you’d walk from your car to the building itself. This way, you’ll know more accurately when you arrive at the meeting location.
Photo: Bogdan Popa/autoevolution This feature is currently in the works, and there is no guarantee that it’ll ever make its way to production. Ideas like this one come and go, and I wouldn’t be surprised to see Apple dropping it. However, considering it has already been added in the iOS 27.3 code, this could be a sign that the feature has made it past the drawing board and could eventually land for all users.
Meanwhile, Google Maps is also offering a similar feature, though it won’t show ETA based on parking data. The application can highlight a building on the map when your destination is that building and provide walking directions from the parking spot to its location.
Like Apple Maps, Google Maps also offers walking and driving directions, so this feature combines both modes for uninterrupted navigation. Once users arrive at the destination where they are supposed to park their cars, Google Maps shows the walking directions, so they continue the journey without entering a new address in the application.
Waze is the only application that can’t get such capabilities because it’s exclusively aimed at drivers. Waze does not support walking, so it always shows the ETA as the point on the map where you are supposed to drive. It can also indicate nearby parking, but it doesn’t offer any walking directions afterwards.
Apple Maps is still working on the detailed city experience that includes more detailed maps, improved navigation, and a redesigned CarPlay experience. The rollout of this feature started in 2021 but is still underway, with Apple seemingly taking its time to bring the new maps to more locations worldwide.
The highly detailed maps were supposed to turn Apple Maps into a fully-featured Google Maps alternative, but considering the slow rollout - most of which is aimed at American regions - many users decided to stick with Google Maps.
Photo: Bogdan Popa/autoevolution Google itself is now in the process of rolling out a similar update called immersive navigation . Google Maps is getting detailed maps with crosswalks and sidewalks, as well as see-through overpasses and 3D buildings similar to those integrated into Apple’s detailed city experience. Google’s new experience is live in the United States and Canada and should arrive in the rest of the world at some point next month.
Apple has so far remained tight-lipped on this new feature spotted in Apple Maps, and I wouldn’t expect the company to say anything about it until it goes live for production users. Apple may be working on parking-aware ETAs. iOS 27.3 adds a TimeToPark flag. When enabled, CoreRoutine uses background location and motion data to measure how long you spent near your destination before parking, and how long you walked afterwards. It saves both metrics per trip, grouped by day of the week and hour. The feature can only be enabled on internal installs, and no Maps feature uses the data yet. — pdfu (@itspdfu) November 9, 2026
